test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 20 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: As per the Scheduled Castes (Rationalisation of Reservation) Act, 2025 implemented by Telangana government, what percentage of reservation will Group II get within the 15 percent quota for SC?
solution:
The correct answer is __**0.09**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Scheduled Castes (Rationalisation of Reservation) Act, 2025** was implemented by the **Telangana government** to ensure equitable distribution of reservation among various sub-groups within the **Scheduled Castes (SC)** category.
 
• Under this act, the SC reservation quota of **15 percent** is further divided into sub-categories to provide fair representation to marginalized sub-groups.
 
• As per the act, **Group II** of the Scheduled Castes has been allocated a specific percentage of the overall SC quota, amounting to **0.09** (or 9 percent).
 
• This law aims to address the long-standing issue of unequal representation within the SC category by ensuring that all sub-groups receive their due share of opportunities.
 
• This reservation policy is part of the government’s broader initiative to promote **social justice** and reduce disparities among socially disadvantaged groups.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Key characteristics of the Scheduled Castes (Rationalisation of Reservation) Act**__

 __
 
• The act was introduced to address **intra-caste inequalities** within the Scheduled Castes.
 
• It provides a mechanism for ensuring that **historically disadvantaged sub-groups** receive adequate representation.
 
• This policy is in alignment with the **constitutional mandate of equality** and affirmative action for disadvantaged communities.
 
 
 
• **Reservation System in India**__
 
 
• The reservation system in India is governed by provisions in the **Indian Constitution** under Articles **15(4), 16(4), and 46.**
 
• It aims to ensure **social and educational empowerment** of Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled Tribes (STs), and Other Backward Classes (OBCs).
 
• Reservation is provided in **government jobs, educational institutions, and legislatures** to address historical inequalities and discrimination.
